summary: The board-specific logic in this core is organised around MAME's gaelco driver, not the Gaelco PCB. The tile priority is MAME's screen_update draw sequence turned into a 16-entry rank table. The sprite engine walks sprite RAM with draw_sprites' exact loop bounds, field extraction and magic numbers. The VRAM decryptor is a line-by-line transliteration of gaelcrpt.cpp's decrypt(). The raster timing is a generic parameterised counter sized to MAME's 320x240 visible area, and nothing in the core is named after board chips, PALs or nets.

findings.signal: priority table = MAME tilemap draw order
findings.note: rank(layer, pen[3], category) gives 16 ranks whose order is exactly the 16 tilemap draw() calls of screen_update_squash (L1 LAYER1, L1 LAYER0, L0 LAYER1, L0 LAYER0 per category, with category 1 interleaved the same way). pen[3] stands in for MAME's 0xff01/0x00ff split transmask. The ordering was copied from a sibling game's MAME update function, not from the hardware's mixer logic.

The state machine starts at spr_idx=2043 (0x800-4-1), steps down by 4 while >=7 (so the last entry is 3), and reads words i, i+2 and i+3 while skipping i+1. This is MAME's `for (i = 0x800-4-1; i >= 3; i -= 4)` loop rerun once per scanline.

The engine uses sy = 240 - y, x = sx - 0x0f + cell*8, the forced priority 4 when color >= 0x38 (m_sprite_palette_force_high), number &= ~3 for 16x16 sprites, and xoff {0,2} / yoff {0,1} with the flip swap. All of these match MAME's code expressions and member defaults one for one.

It has the same swap/type selectors, the four bitswap<16> tables, the k-bit selections, the 6-bit and 5-bit masked adds, the param1/param2 XORs and the final bitswap, all in MAME's order. The output is unused here (vmem_dec_wdata = oEdb in biomtoy_main.v:112; MAME's maniacsq map is unencrypted too), so the module was carried over from a MAME-modelled sibling core.

findings.signal: tile fetch uses MAME gfx-element conventions
findings.note: code = 0x4000 + data[15:2] reproduces MAME's tileinfo.set(1, 0x4000 + code, ...) gfx-index offset. The ROM address {code,5'b0} + {col[3],row} follows tilelayout16's STEP8(16*8,1) half-tile split, not a board fetch sequence.

This compiled but uninstantiated module computes ROM addresses for MAME's two gfx layouts (8x8 at code*8, 16x16 at code*32). It is organised around MAME's GFXDECODE entries rather than the board's ROM addressing.

findings.signal: generic raster timing sized to MAME visarea
findings.note: A VGA-style parameterised counter (HVIS/HFP/HSW/HBP) generates hpos/vpos. Scroll is hpos+vreg+3 / vpos+vreg+16, i.e. MAME's visible-area offset of 16 plus hand-tuned constants. No H/V counter bits from the board drive the fetch phases.

There is one equality-compare chip select per MAME map line (DSW2 at 0x700000, DSW1 at 0x700002, okibank at 0x70000d, oki at 0x70000f, irqack at 0x10800c). It also has an LS259-style outlatch at 0x70000b/select 0x70 taken from squash/thoop_map, which maniacsq_map lacks. Its flip_screen output is left unconnected.

findings.signal: OKI bank window as MAME oki_map
findings.note: core_addr < 0x30000 goes direct, and above that okibank is concatenated with A[15:0]. This repeats MAME's map ranges as a magnitude compare, but any correct core needs this banking.

findings.signal: sprite line buffers and SDRAM-fed per-pixel tile pipeline
findings.note: Double-banked 320-entry line buffers, latency shift registers and ce_pix pipelines are standard FPGA engineering. Sprite priority bits are stored in the line buffer but never used in the final mix (biomtoy_video_top.v:86-89 just overlays any non-zero sprite pen).
These are a renamed jtframe 68k DTACK/clock-enable generator, the fx68k CPU, the jt6295 OKI and an xBGR555 palette split. They say nothing about provenance.
